lessons.title: Describe a scene
lessons.summary: “The door's open”, “There's a photo on the wall”, “She said with a smile”: describe how things are, and how people do things.
lessons.topic: {{着|zhe}}: a state that lasts ({{门开着|mén kāizhe}}); place + verb + {{着|zhe}} + thing ({{墙上挂着一张画|qiáng shang guàzhe yì zhāng huà}}); verb + {{着|zhe}} + verb ({{笑着说|xiàozhe shuō}})

goal.r: Qiáng shang guàzhe yì zhāng quánjiāfú.
goal.tr: There's a family photo hanging on the wall.

dialog.r: Qǐng jìn! Mén kāizhe ne.
dialog.tr: Come in! The door's open.

dialog.t: 哇，你的家真漂亮！墙上挂着很多照片。
dialog.r: Wā, nǐ de jiā zhēn piàoliang! Qiáng shang guàzhe hěn duō zhàopiàn.
dialog.tr: Wow, your place is lovely! There are lots of photos on the wall.

dialog.t: 都是我们家的。你坐着，我去泡茶。
dialog.r: Dōu shì wǒmen jiā de. Nǐ zuòzhe, wǒ qù pào chá.
dialog.tr: They're all of my family. Sit down, I'll go and make some tea.

dialog.r: Zhuōzi shang fàngzhe shénme?
dialog.tr: What's that on the table?

dialog.t: 那是我奶奶送我的花瓶。
dialog.r: Nà shì wǒ nǎinai sòng wǒ de huāpíng.
dialog.tr: That's a vase my grandma gave me.

blocks.p: **A state that lasts: verb + {{着|zhe}}.** {{在|zài}} says an action is going on; {{着|zhe}} says the state it leaves behind stays: {{门开着。|Mén kāizhe.}} “The door is open” (someone opened it, and it stays open). {{灯开着。|Dēng kāizhe.}} “The light's on.” {{他穿着一件红衣服。|Tā chuānzhe yí jiàn hóng yīfu.}} “He's wearing a red top.”

**Painting a place: place + verb + {{着|zhe}} + thing.** It's like the place + {{有|yǒu}} you know, but the verb paints the picture: {{墙上挂着一张画。|Qiáng shang guàzhe yì zhāng huà.}} “There's a painting hanging on the wall.” {{门口站着一个人。|Ménkǒu zhànzhe yí ge rén.}} “Someone is standing at the door.”

table: There's a painting on the wall.
There's a book on the table.
Someone is standing at the door.
A cat is sitting on the chair.

blocks.p: **Doing one thing in a certain way: verb + {{着|zhe}} + verb.** The first verb, with {{着|zhe}}, says how the second is done: {{她笑着说|tā xiàozhe shuō}} “she said with a smile”, {{我们走着去吧。|Wǒmen zǒuzhe qù ba.}} “Let's walk there.” {{别躺着看书。|Bié tǎngzhe kàn shū.}} “Don't read lying down.”

ex.r: Qiáng shang guàzhe yì zhāng quánjiāfú.
ex.tr: There's a family photo hanging on the wall.

ex.r: Tā chuānzhe yí jiàn hóng yīfu.
Zhuōzi shang fàngzhe yí ge huāpíng.
ex.tr: There's a vase on the table.
She said with a smile, “It's fine.”

ex.r: Wǒmen zǒuzhe qù ba, bù yuǎn.

blocks.tip: {{着|zhe}} is the word for describing photos and scenes. Look around you and try it: {{窗外下着雨。|Chuāng wài xiàzhe yǔ.}} “It's raining outside the window.”

mistakes.tr: There's a painting on the wall.
mistakes.why: The verb + {{着|zhe}} takes the place of {{有|yǒu}}: not both. {{墙上挂着一张画。|Qiáng shang guàzhe yì zhāng huà.}}

mistakes.tr: There's a painting on the wall.
mistakes.why: To describe a place, start with the place, as with {{有|yǒu}}.

lessons.title: Tell a story
lessons.summary: “That day it was pouring… Suddenly… In the end…”: tell what happened, in order, so people want to hear the end.
lessons.topic: The past in order: {{那天|nà tiān}}, {{突然|tūrán}}, {{后来|hòulái}}, {{结果|jiéguǒ}}, {{最后|zuìhòu}}; {{就|jiù}} (already) and {{才|cái}} (not until)

goal.t: 我们等了一个小时，他才来。
goal.r: Wǒmen děng le yí ge xiǎoshí, tā cái lái.
goal.tr: We waited an hour before he finally turned up.

dialog.t: 昨天我去机场接我妈妈。
dialog.r: Zuótiān wǒ qù jīchǎng jiē wǒ māma.
dialog.tr: Yesterday I went to the airport to pick up my mum.

dialog.r: Ránhòu ne?
dialog.tr: And then?

dialog.t: 飞机晚点了，我等了三个小时，她晚上十一点才到。
dialog.r: Fēijī wǎndiǎn le, wǒ děng le sān ge xiǎoshí, tā wǎnshang shíyī diǎn cái dào.
dialog.tr: The flight was delayed, I waited three hours, and she didn't land until eleven.

dialog.r: Tiān a!
dialog.tr: Oh no!

dialog.t: 后来我们打车回家，突然下起了大雨，结果司机走错了路！
dialog.r: Hòulái wǒmen dǎchē huí jiā, tūrán xiàqǐ le dàyǔ, jiéguǒ sījī zǒucuò le lù!
dialog.tr: Then we took a taxi home, it suddenly started pouring, and the driver went the wrong way!

dialog.r: Nǐmen jǐ diǎn dào jiā de?
dialog.tr: What time did you get home?

dialog.r: Yì diǎn duō cái dào!
dialog.tr: Not until after one!

blocks.p: **Setting the scene and moving on.** A story starts with when ({{那天|nà tiān}} “that day”, {{上个周末|shàng ge zhōumò}} “last weekend”) and moves on with linking words. Each event takes its {{了|le}}; descriptions and the background don't.

table: {{那天天气很好。|Nà tiān tiānqì hěn hǎo.}}
{{后来我们去吃饭了。|Hòulái wǒmen qù chīfàn le.}}
and so, as it turned out
{{结果我们迷路了。|Jiéguǒ wǒmen mílù le.}}
{{最后我们到家了。|Zuìhòu wǒmen dào jiā le.}}

blocks.p: **{{就|jiù}} and {{才|cái}}: earlier or later than expected.** Before the verb, {{就|jiù}} means “already, as early as”, and {{才|cái}} “not until, only then”: {{他八点就到了。|Tā bā diǎn jiù dào le.}} “He was already there at eight.” {{他十点才到。|Tā shí diǎn cái dào.}} “He didn't arrive until ten.” {{才|cái}} takes no {{了|le}}.

ex.t: 我们等了一个小时，他才来。
ex.r: Wǒmen děng le yí ge xiǎoshí, tā cái lái.
ex.tr: We waited an hour before he finally turned up.

ex.t: 那天下着大雨，路上一个人也没有。
ex.r: Nà tiān xiàzhe dàyǔ, lù shang yí ge rén yě méiyǒu.
ex.tr: That day it was pouring, and there wasn't a soul on the street.

ex.r: Wǒ zǎoshang liù diǎn jiù qǐchuáng le.
ex.tr: I was up at six this morning.

ex.t: 我们走了很久，结果走错了！
ex.r: Wǒmen zǒu le hěn jiǔ, jiéguǒ zǒucuò le!
ex.tr: We walked for ages, and it turned out we'd gone the wrong way!

ex.t: 最后，我们十二点才到家。
ex.r: Zuìhòu, wǒmen shí'èr diǎn cái dào jiā.
ex.tr: In the end, we didn't get home until twelve.

blocks.tip: Listeners keep a story going with {{然后呢？|Ránhòu ne?}} “And then?”, {{真的吗？|Zhēn de ma?}} “Really?” and {{天啊！|Tiān a!}} “Oh my!” Use them when a friend tells you one.

mistakes.why: {{才|cái}} takes no {{了|le}}: {{他十点才到。|Tā shí diǎn cái dào.}}

mistakes.tr: The weather was lovely that day.
mistakes.why: The background takes no {{了|le}}: only the events do.

lessons.title: Say how things are changing
lessons.summary: “Your Chinese is getting better and better”, “The more I learn, the more I like it”, “He's become very busy”: talk about change.
lessons.topic: {{越来越|yuè lái yuè}} + adjective; {{越…越…|yuè… yuè…}}; {{变得|biàn de}} + adjective; {{比以前|bǐ yǐqián}}

goal.r: Nǐ de Zhōngwén yuè lái yuè hǎo le!
goal.tr: Your Chinese is getting better and better!

dialog.t: 好久不见！你的中文越来越好了！
dialog.r: Hǎojiǔ bú jiàn! Nǐ de Zhōngwén yuè lái yuè hǎo le!
dialog.tr: Long time no see! Your Chinese is getting better and better!

dialog.r: Xièxie! Wǒ yuè xué yuè xǐhuan.
dialog.tr: Thanks! The more I learn, the more I like it.

dialog.r: Běijīng yě biàn le hěn duō ba?
dialog.tr: Beijing has changed a lot too, hasn't it?

dialog.t: 对，地铁越来越方便，可是房子越来越贵了。
dialog.r: Duì, dìtiě yuè lái yuè fāngbiàn, kěshì fángzi yuè lái yuè guì le.
dialog.tr: Yes, the subway gets more and more convenient, but flats get more and more expensive.

dialog.t: 是啊，生活比以前好多了，也比以前忙多了！
dialog.r: Shì a, shēnghuó bǐ yǐqián hǎo duō le, yě bǐ yǐqián máng duō le!
dialog.tr: True, life's much better than it was, and much busier too!

blocks.p: **More and more: {{越来越|yuè lái yuè}} + adjective.** {{天气越来越冷了。|Tiānqì yuè lái yuè lěng le.}} “It's getting colder and colder.” There's no {{很|hěn}}, as after {{比|bǐ}}, and often the {{了|le}} of change at the end.

**The more…, the more…: {{越|yuè}}… {{越|yuè}}….** Each {{越|yuè}} goes right before a verb or an adjective: {{我越学越喜欢。|Wǒ yuè xué yuè xǐhuan.}} “The more I learn, the more I like it.” {{雨越下越大。|Yǔ yuè xià yuè dà.}} “The rain is getting heavier and heavier.” With two people: {{你越说，他越生气。|Nǐ yuè shuō, tā yuè shēngqì.}} “The more you talk, the angrier he gets.”

**Become: {{变得|biàn de}}** + adjective: {{他变得很瘦。|Tā biàn de hěn shòu.}} “He's become very thin.” And to compare with the past, {{比以前|bǐ yǐqián}}: {{我比以前忙。|Wǒ bǐ yǐqián máng.}} “I'm busier than I used to be.”

blocks.p: **Passing on words is easy in Chinese.** Nothing changes: no tenses to shift, no “that”. Say who said it, then their words, from your own point of view: {{他说：“我不来了。”|Tā shuō: “Wǒ bù lái le.”}} becomes {{他说他不来了。|Tā shuō tā bù lái le.}} “He said he isn't coming.”

**Telling, and asking someone to do something.** {{告诉|gàosu}} “tell” + the person + the news: {{他告诉我他要结婚了。|Tā gàosu wǒ tā yào jiéhūn le.}} “He told me he's getting married.” {{让|ràng}} + the person + what to do: {{妈妈让我买牛奶。|Māma ràng wǒ mǎi niúnǎi.}} “Mum asked me to buy milk.”

**Passing on a question**: {{问|wèn}} “ask” + the person + the question, without {{吗|ma}}. A yes-or-no question becomes A-not-A: {{她问你周末有没有空。|Tā wèn nǐ zhōumò yǒu méiyǒu kòng.}} “She asked if you're free at the weekend.” A question word stays where it is: {{他问我几点到。|Tā wèn wǒ jǐ diǎn dào.}} “He asked me what time I'd get there.”

lessons.title: Imagine and wish
lessons.summary: “If I were you, I'd take a day off”, “If only I had more time!”, “Get well soon”: imagine, wish and hope.
lessons.topic: {{如果我是你|rúguǒ wǒ shì nǐ}}; {{要是…就好了|yàoshi… jiù hǎo le}} “if only”; {{希望|xīwàng}}; {{真想|zhēn xiǎng}}

blocks.p: **No special verbs for imagining.** English changes its verbs to imagine (“if I *were*”, “I *would*”). Chinese uses the same {{如果|rúguǒ}} / {{要是|yàoshi}} … {{就|jiù}} as for real conditions, and the situation makes it clear: {{如果我是你，我就去。|Rúguǒ wǒ shì nǐ, wǒ jiù qù.}} “If I were you, I'd go.”

**If only…! {{要是…就好了|yàoshi… jiù hǎo le}}**, around what you wish were true: {{要是我有更多时间就好了！|Yàoshi wǒ yǒu gèng duō shíjiān jiù hǎo le!}} It works for the past too: {{要是我早点儿来就好了。|Yàoshi wǒ zǎo diǎnr lái jiù hǎo le.}} “If only I'd come earlier.”

**Hoping and longing.** {{希望|xīwàng}} “hope” + a whole sentence: {{希望你早日康复！|Xīwàng nǐ zǎorì kāngfù!}} “Get well soon!” {{真想|zhēn xiǎng}} “really want to, I'd love to”: {{我真想去云南看看！|Wǒ zhēn xiǎng qù Yúnnán kànkan!}} “I'd love to visit Yunnan!”

blocks.p: **{{呢|ne}}: and you? what about…?** After a noun or a pronoun, {{呢|ne}} turns the talk to it: {{我很好，你呢？|Wǒ hěn hǎo, nǐ ne?}} After a whole question, it sounds softer and more curious: {{你在想什么呢？|Nǐ zài xiǎng shénme ne?}} “What are you thinking about?”

**{{吧|ba}}: I suppose, right?** A statement + {{吧|ba}} checks something you think is true: {{你是美国人吧？|Nǐ shì Měiguórén ba?}} “You're American, I take it?” It's softer than {{吗|ma}}, which asks without guessing. {{对吧？|Duì ba?}} and {{是吧？|Shì ba?}} at the end are “right?”, “isn't it?”.

**{{啊|a}}: warmth and feeling.** {{啊|a}} at the end makes a sentence friendlier, or more emotional: {{好啊！|Hǎo a!}} “Sure!”, {{真漂亮啊！|Zhēn piàoliang a!}} “It's so beautiful!” In writing you'll also see {{呀|ya}}, the same word after some vowels: {{好呀|hǎo ya}}.

**Reacting**: {{是吗？|Shì ma?}} “Really?”, {{真的吗？|Zhēn de ma?}} “Really?!”, {{原来是这样！|Yuánlái shì zhèyàng!}} “Oh, I see!” ({{原来|yuánlái}} “so it turns out”), and {{怪不得|guàibude}} “no wonder”: {{怪不得你中文这么好！|Guàibude nǐ Zhōngwén zhème hǎo!}}

table: {{我喝茶，你呢？|Wǒ hē chá, nǐ ne?}}
I'm having tea. What about you?
{{明天放假，对吧？|Míngtiān fàngjià, duì ba?}}
{{原来你是老师！|Yuánlái nǐ shì lǎoshī!}}

ex.r: Nǐ lèi le ba? Xiūxi yíxià ba.
ex.tr: You must be tired. Have a rest.
No wonder your Chinese is so good!

blocks.tip: These little words are what make Chinese sound alive. Listen for them in films and conversations, and try one in every chat: a {{呢|ne}} to turn the question back, a {{吧|ba}} to guess, an {{啊|a}} to sound warm.

mistakes.why: One ending is enough: {{吧|ba}} (guessing) or {{吗|ma}} (just asking), never both.
{{呢|ne}} goes after the word it's about: {{你呢？|nǐ ne?}}

practice.q: You think your new colleague is from Shanghai, and want to check. You say…
options: {{你是上海人吧？|Nǐ shì Shànghǎirén ba?}}
{{你是上海人呢？|Nǐ shì Shànghǎirén ne?}}
{{上海人你是吗？|Shànghǎirén nǐ shì ma?}}
practice.why: Checking a guess: {{吧|ba}}.

practice.q: A friend says their mum is Chinese. “No wonder your Chinese is so good!” is…
options: {{怪不得你中文这么好！|Guàibude nǐ Zhōngwén zhème hǎo!}}
{{原来你中文这么好吗！|Yuánlái nǐ Zhōngwén zhème hǎo ma!}}
practice.why: “No wonder”: {{怪不得|guàibude}}.

practice.q: Chatting at a party. Choose your replies.

lines.t: 我下个月要去美国工作。
lines.r: Wǒ xià ge yuè yào qù Měiguó gōngzuò.
lines.tr: I'm going to work in America next month.

lines.why: “Really?” is {{是吗？|Shì ma?}} ({{是吧|shì ba}} would be “right?”, checking a guess.)

lines.r: Niǔyuē. Nǐ qù guo Niǔyuē, duì ba?
lines.tr: New York. You've been to New York, right?

options: 对，去过两次。你呢？第一次去吗？
对，去过两次。呢你？第一次去吗？
rs: Duì, qù guo liǎng cì. Nǐ ne? Dì yī cì qù ma?
Duì, qù guo liǎng cì. Ne nǐ? Dì yī cì qù ma?
lines.why: {{你呢？|Nǐ ne?}} turns the question back to them.

practice.q: Put the words in order.
React to surprising news: “Oh, I see!”
Your turn: someone tells you {{我在学英语。|Wǒ zài xué Yīngyǔ.}} React, make a guess about them with {{吧|ba}}, and turn the question back with {{呢|ne}}.

answers.t: 是吗？你想去美国吧？我在学中文呢！
answers.r: Shì ma? Nǐ xiǎng qù Měiguó ba? Wǒ zài xué Zhōngwén ne!
answers.tr: Really? You're thinking of going to America, I suppose? I'm learning Chinese!

answers.t: 真的吗？你英语说得很好吧！我在学中文，你呢，学了多长时间了？
answers.r: Zhēn de ma? Nǐ Yīngyǔ shuō de hěn hǎo ba! Wǒ zài xué Zhōngwén, nǐ ne, xué le duō cháng shíjiān le?
answers.tr: Really? I bet you speak it well! I'm learning Chinese. And you, how long have you been learning?
